answer: Before an agent can earn fees, it must lock a bond that is slashed if its work is caught violating the market’s rules; payments accrue only after independent reviewers confirm useful output. One person can still create a canyon of fake identities, but each must tie up capital and pass the same checks, while coordinated fraud risks losing every bond. A pigment sample may be cheap to copy, and a fable can sound convincing, but neither makes a Sybil identity profitable when detection carries a real financial penalty.
